result.summary: The intersection features a marked zebra crosswalk and a large concrete refuge island, but its safety is significantly compromised by a large vehicle parked on the pedestrian space. The lack of visible pedestrian signals and the presence of cracked pavement further reduce the quality of the walking environment.

hazards.name: Large Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: A large green truck is parked on the concrete refuge island, blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians and obstructing the walking path.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image on the concrete island

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signals are visible at this signalized intersection, which can lead to confusion about crossing phases.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection corners

hazards.name: Degraded Pavement
hazards.description: The road surface in and around the crosswalk shows significant cracking and wear, posing a potential tripping hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and crosswalk area

interventions.title: Parking Enforcement and Bollards
interventions.description: Install bollards on the refuge island to prevent illegal parking and ensure the space remains clear for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-specific signals to the existing traffic light poles to provide clear guidance for crossing.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked pavement to eliminate tripping hazards and improve the overall quality of the crossing.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, multi-lane arterial road with a marked bike lane but no visible pedestrian crossing infrastructure. The environment is dominated by vehicle traffic with long, unprotected crossing distances and a lack of traffic calming measures.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a refuge island or median.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire width of the roadway

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross this wide arterial road.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible stretch of the road

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the left curb line may obscure pedestrians attempting to cross from the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossings with high-visibility paint and add signage to alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential urban intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including a marked zebra crosswalk and a curb ramp with tactile warning pads. While sidewalks are present and continuous, the environment lacks active traffic control signals and features some visual obstructions from parked vehicles near the corner.

hazards.name: Faded Pavement Markings
hazards.description: The zebra crosswalk markings are visibly worn and peeling, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway crossing

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection on the side street may block sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb of the side street

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility thermoplastic markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to improve sightlines for both pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and physically prevent parking too close to the intersection.

result.summary: The intersection provides essential pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. However, the wide multi-lane one-way street creates a significant crossing distance without a refuge island, potentially exposing pedestrians to higher-speed traffic.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross three travel lanes and a bike lane in a single stage without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground crossing the main roadway

hazards.name: High-speed roadway design
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane one-way configuration is designed for high vehicle throughput, which often encourages higher speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway stretching into the background

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the intersection corners to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Construct a raised island between travel lanes to provide a safe waiting area for pedestrians mid-crossing.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic receives a green light.
